chunks: And from him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Zurara, who said:

I saw a son of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) during the life of Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who was called 'Abdullah al-Fayim', who had grown up. I said to him, 'O boy, who is the one beside you, a master to them?' He said, 'This is my master.' The master said to him, teasing him, 'I am not a master to you.' He said, 'That is worse for you,' and he thrust his spear into the boy's funeral shroud, so he died. He was taken out in a basket to al-Baqi', and Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) came out wearing a yellow silk tunic, a yellow silk turban, and a yellow silk edge. He walked towards al-Baqi', leaning on me, while the people consoled him on the death of his grandson. When he reached al-Baqi', Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) stepped forward and prayed over him, saying 'Allahu Akbar' four times over him. Then he ordered that he be buried. Then he took my hands, moved aside with me, and said, 'Indeed, prayer was not performed over children. Rather, the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) would order them to be buried behind, behind, and not pray over them. And I prayed over him on account of the people of the city, lest they say,

key_terms.أَبْنُ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Son of Abu Abdillah (Imam Muhammad al-Baqir)

ai.seo_question: Why did Imam al-Baqir perform funeral prayer over his grandson despite the practice of Imam Ali?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights the pragmatic flexibility of Imam al-Baqir in adapting ritual practice to social context, specifically performing the funeral prayer over his grandson to prevent the people of Medina from claiming the Imams neglected their own kin. It contrasts the established practice of Imam Ali, who buried children without prayer, with the Imam's deliberate choice to align with communal expectations, illustrating the principle of *takhfif* (ease) and *mu'aradhat al-nas* (avoiding public criticism) in Shia jurisprudence.
